mainEntity.name: How many implants are needed for a full mouth?

acceptedAnswer.text: The number of implants depends on the clinical approach, your bone support, and the type of restoration planned. Full arch restorations typically use several implants per jaw, but the exact number is determined during the assessment and planning stage.

mainEntity.name: Are full mouth dental implants permanent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full mouth implant restorations are designed as fixed, long-term restorations. The implants integrate with the jawbone and the prosthetic teeth are secured in place. However, the prosthetic components may require maintenance, adjustments, or replacement over time due to normal wear.

mainEntity.name: How long does full mouth implant treatment take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment typically spans several months, including the healing period required for the implants to integrate with the jawbone. The exact timeline depends on whether preparatory procedures are needed and how the healing progresses. Your dental team will provide estimated timescales during planning.

mainEntity.name: How much do full mouth implants cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Costs vary significantly depending on the number of implants, the type of restoration, any preparatory treatments needed, and the complexity of the case. A consultation and clinical assessment are necessary to provide an accurate, personalised treatment plan and cost breakdown.

mainEntity.name: How do you clean full mouth dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full mouth implant restorations are cleaned with a soft-bristled toothbrush, interdental brushes, and water flossers. Cleaning beneath fixed bridge frameworks is particularly important. Regular professional hygiene appointments complement your daily routine and help maintain the health of the surrounding tissue.

mainEntity.name: Is full mouth implant treatment painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant placement is carried out under local anaesthetic, so you should not feel pain during the procedure. Some discomfort, swelling, or bruising may occur in the days following surgery, but this is typically manageable and resolves within a short period.
